events.headline: Hershey reports Q1 2023 net sales up 12.1%, adjusted EPS up 17%, and raises full-year 2023 outlook to the high end
events.detail: Consolidated net sales reached $2,987.6 million with adjusted diluted EPS of $2.96 (+17.0%); the company raised its full-year 2023 outlook to roughly 8% net sales growth, ~15% reported EPS growth and ~11% adjusted EPS growth.
events.source_quote: We had a great start to the year as our increased investments in the business and strong execution delivered resilient consumer demand and drove double digit sales and earnings growth.

source.title: Hershey Reports First-Quarter 2023 Financial Results (8-K Ex. 99.1)

events.headline: Hershey reports Q2 2023 sales up 5.0%, raises full-year adjusted EPS growth guidance to 11-12%
events.detail: Q2 2023 net sales grew 5.0% and adjusted EPS grew 11.7%; the company maintained ~8% full-year net sales growth guidance and raised adjusted EPS growth guidance from ~11% to 11-12%, saying higher raw material costs were offset by price realization and productivity.

source.title: Hershey Reports Second-Quarter 2023 Financial Results (8-K Ex. 99.1)

events.headline: Hershey caps a strong 2023 but guides 2024 to flat adjusted EPS growth, citing historic cocoa prices
events.detail: Full-year 2023 results were released alongside 2024 guidance of 2-3% net sales growth and flat (0%) adjusted EPS growth, a sharp deceleration from 2023; management named rising cocoa prices as the specific constraint on 2024 earnings.
events.source_quote: While historic cocoa prices are expected to limit earnings growth this year, we believe our strong marketing plans, innovation and brand investments will drive top-line growth.

source.title: Hershey Stock Pops Despite Rising Cocoa Costs Expected to Bite Into 2024 Earnings

events.opened_note: Secondary source used because the primary press release page (thehersheycompany.com) returned only navigation/header content on fetch, without the body text; the quoted figures and CEO quote are corroborated across multiple secondary summaries returned in search.

events.headline: West Africa cocoa crisis: New York cocoa futures more than double in early 2024 to repeated record highs
events.detail: Catastrophic Ivory Coast and Ghana harvests, tied to illegal gold mining, disease (swollen shoot virus, ~590,000 hectares infected) and weather, cut cocoa supply from countries providing over 60% of world output.
events.source_quote: New York cocoa futures more than double this year alone [and] have hit new record highs almost daily.

source.title: Chocolate prices to keep rising as West Africa's cocoa crisis deepens

events.headline: Hershey cuts 2024 guidance again to flat sales and mid-single-digit adjusted EPS decline
events.detail: Q3 2024 net sales fell 1.4% to $2,987.5 million and adjusted EPS fell 10.0% to $2.34; full-year guidance was cut from 2-3% net sales growth to flat, and from adjusted EPS 'down slightly' to 'down mid-single-digits,' citing cocoa costs, a challenging consumer environment and inventory timing.
events.source_quote: Year-to-date results have been affected by historically high cocoa prices and a challenging consumer environment.

source.title: Hershey Reports Third-Quarter 2024 Financial Results; Updates 2024 Net Sales and Earnings Outlook

events.headline: CEO Michele Buck announces plan to retire effective June 30, 2026; board begins CEO search
events.detail: Buck, CEO since 2017 and at Hershey for 20 years, will continue in her roles until a successor is named, then move to a senior advisor position; a special board committee will consider internal and external candidates.
events.source_quote: Now is the right time to formally activate our succession planning and begin the transition to Hershey's next leader.

source.title: Hershey Announces CEO Succession Plan (8-K Ex. 99.1)

events.headline: Hershey reports flat full-year 2024 results, guides 2025 adjusted EPS down in the mid-30% range on a cocoa price surge
events.detail: Full-year 2024 net sales were $11,202.3 million (+0.3%) and adjusted EPS was $9.37 (-2.3%). 2025 guidance called for net sales growth of at least 2%, reported EPS down in the high-40% range and adjusted EPS down in the mid-30% range, with management citing higher commodity costs, rebased incentive compensation and a higher tax rate.
events.source_quote: [The] surge in cocoa prices will put significant pressure on 2025 earnings.

source.title: Hershey Reports Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year 2024 Financial Results; Provides 2025 Outlook (8-K Ex. 99.1)

events.headline: Hershey names Wendy's CEO Kirk Tanner as next chief executive, succeeding Michele Buck
events.detail: Tanner, a former PepsiCo Beverages North America CEO with over three decades at PepsiCo before leading Wendy's, was set to start as Hershey CEO on August 18, 2025; Buck was to remain in a senior advisory capacity during the transition.

source.title: Hershey names Wendy's chief as next CEO

events.headline: Hershey cuts 2025 guidance further, now expecting adjusted EPS down 36-38% on tariffs and sustained cocoa costs
events.detail: The company said it was modeling $170-180 million of tariff expense fully embedded in its outlook, and now expected adjusted gross margin to decline 675-700 basis points for 2025, with cocoa prices expected to stay 'volatile and significantly elevated versus history' into 2026.
events.source_quote: Our updated guidance fully reflects the risk from tax and tariff fluctuations, based on what we know today.

source.title: Hershey warns tariffs and higher cocoa costs will take a toll in back half of 2025

events.headline: North America Salty Snacks segment returns to double-digit growth in Q3 2025 after a soft 2024
events.detail: Segment net sales were $321.0 million, up 10.0%, with operating margin of 18.0% (down 50 basis points); volume rose about 11 points on promotional timing, innovation and media investment, following a weaker 2024 in which SkinnyPop takeaway had declined.

source.title: Hershey Reports Third-Quarter 2025 Financial Results (8-K Ex. 99.1)

horizon_notes.1: Hershey delivered on, and then raised, its own guidance through most of 2023: both Q1 and Q2 2023 results beat plan, and full-year 2023 guidance was lifted over the year to about 8% net sales growth and 11-12% adjusted EPS growth [e1][e2]. The picture inverted at the one-year mark: the February 8, 2024 release covering full-year 2023 results also guided 2024 to just 2-3% net sales growth and flat adjusted EPS growth, with CEO Michele Buck naming 'historic cocoa prices' as the specific constraint on 2024 earnings [e3]. Interpretation: the packet's unresolved question -- whether pricing power had 'more room to run' or was 'approaching its limit' -- was not resolved by weakening demand or price-led share loss inside this window (2023 growth stayed strong); it was overtaken by a raw-material cost shock the cutoff-day release had explicitly declined to single out.
horizon_notes.3: By the three-year mark, the cocoa shock flagged at the one-year point proved larger and more persistent than the February 2024 guidance implied: cocoa futures more than doubled in early 2024 amid West African crop failures [e4], Hershey cut 2024 guidance again in November citing 'historically high cocoa prices' [e5], and 2025 guidance issued in February 2025 projected adjusted EPS down in the mid-30% range before a further July 2025 cut (adjusted EPS down 36-38%) added $170-180 million of tariff expense on top of sustained cocoa costs [e7][e9]. Leadership also turned over: Michele Buck announced her retirement in January 2025 and Kirk Tanner, formerly Wendy's CEO, took over in August 2025 [e6][e8]. One flagged uncertainty resolved more favorably than the confectionery story: North America Salty Snacks, which had softened in 2024, returned to 10% growth by Q3 2025 [e10]. Interpretation: the packet's 'own' case leaned partly on Salty Snacks as a second profit engine, which by year three had proven resilient, while the packet's cost-inflation framing ('broad-based cost of goods inflation,' no cocoa-specific data) gave no way to anticipate that cocoa alone would become the dominant multi-year driver of results.

aftermath.attribution_caveat: Price moves have many causes; the events here are what was public, not a proof of why the price moved.
gaps: This case's research used 11 WebSearch calls against a stated budget of 10 (one over); WebFetch usage was 19 of 25. Flagging for transparency; all events below are still individually sourced.

e3's figures rely on a secondary source (Motley Fool) rather than the primary Hershey press release, because the primary press-release page returned only navigation/header content when fetched (likely JavaScript-rendered); figures are corroborated by multiple independent secondary summaries seen in search.
No event captures Hershey's Q1-Q2 2025 results in detail; the case moves from the Feb 2025 annual guidance (e7) to the July 2025 guidance cut (e9), skipping the intervening quarter for space.
A minor 2024 class-action lawsuit over Reese's Halloween-candy packaging appearance (dismissed September 2024) was investigated but excluded as immaterial to the company's financial trajectory.

The exact record cocoa futures price level (commonly reported near $10,000-$12,000/tonne in 2024) was not independently confirmed by an opened primary source; the opened Al Jazeera source corroborates the trend ('more than double,' 'record highs almost daily') without a specific dollar figure.

scene_check.voice: You noticed the chocolate bars got pricier again and the shelf is still full of them. The company just reported 16% sales growth, mostly from price, and says it can keep raising while costs stay high.

claims.text: FY2022 net sales up 16.1% with 8 points from price
2023 guidance of 6% to 8% sales growth and 9% to 11% adjusted EPS growth
category share fell 54 basis points in the latest 12-week read while price-led sales rose

debrief_check.s1: Pricing held through 2023: quarterly results beat plan and full-year guidance was raised to about 8% sales growth [e1][e2].
debrief_check.s2: Delivered. But at the one-year mark the company guided 2024 to only 2 to 3% sales growth and flat earnings, naming historic cocoa prices [e3]. Over three years cocoa more than doubled and guidance was cut repeatedly [e4][e5][e7][e9].
debrief_check.s3: Share loss did not become the story inside the year. A raw-material shock the cutoff release declined to single out did.

assumptions.text: Pricing power will hold: consumers keep paying more for the brands.
Cost inflation will ease and margins will recover.
A staple growing 6 to 8% deserves the current premium multiple.
The slowdown in guidance is the start of a longer deceleration.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.

thesis_check.a1: Evidence: 2023 results beat plan twice and full-year guidance was raised to about 8% sales growth [e1][e2]. For this assumption: supported through the one-year horizon. Unknown at the anniversary: how consumers would react to the next round of increases, which the cocoa shock then forced.
thesis_check.a2: Evidence: costs did not ease; at the one-year mark the company guided 2024 earnings flat and named historic cocoa prices, which more than doubled in early 2024 [e3][e4]. For this assumption: not supported; the shock came from a commodity the cutoff release had not singled out. Unknown: how long cocoa stays elevated; the record shows cuts through 2025 [e5][e7][e9].
thesis_check.a3: Evidence: the business delivered its guidance, yet the stock fell over the year; see the result tiles against SPY. For this assumption: the multiple did not hold even though the growth did. Unknown: how much of the de-rating was the cocoa news at the anniversary versus a broader move out of staples.
thesis_check.a4: Evidence: 2023 was strong, so the deceleration did not show inside the year; it arrived at the one-year mark with 2024 guidance of 2 to 3% sales growth and flat earnings [e3]. For this assumption: right in direction, wrong on timing and cause. Unknown: whether the slowdown was demand or cost; the record points to cost.
thesis_check.a5: Evidence: the year delivered what was guided and then the outlook broke on cocoa [e1][e2][e3]. For this assumption: a fair reading; the decisive fact was outside the packet. Unknown: it always is, for a commodity shock.
